title: The Night Owl
logline: The foggiest night of the year, and the lighthouse keeper is a tiny old owl who cannot keep her eyes open. A ferry is feeling its way toward the rocks. {{product.name}} keeps the light on.

lore: Mabel has kept Point Hollow Light for 52 years, and her mother kept it before her; a portrait of her mother in a keeper's cap hangs by the stairs.
Point Hollow is a lump of black rock three miles off the fishing town of Grey Harbor. The lens must be wound by hand every hour or it slows and dims.
Every ship she sees safely past gets one chalk tally mark on the curved lamp-room wall; after 52 years the marks climb higher than she is able to reach, so the newest ones are tiny and low.

Captain Teo Reyes has run the Marigold, the last ferry of the night, for 18 years. Every Sunday he sends a slatted wooden crate of supplies and groceries, packed in ice or straw, up to the gallery on a rope pulley, and they have never met face to face.
Tonight is the thickest fog in forty years, and the Marigold is carrying twelve passengers home from the harvest fair.

beats.summary: Mabel's huge eyes droop shut as the lamp behind her flickers; she tells herself to stay awake.
Outside, the beam is dying in the fog while the ferry creeps toward the rocks; the captain radios in; Mabel jolts awake.
She digs the product out of the Sunday crate (at true scale beside a 30 cm owl), uses it, and her eyes pop wide. The product line.
She throws her whole body on the crank, the lens roars to full blaze, the beam slices the fog and the ferry turns away from the rocks.
The ferry passes safely below, passengers wave lanterns, Mabel waves back from the gallery.
Sunrise: the product on the gallery ledge, Mabel finally asleep in her blanket beside it. Tagline.
